summary: Gavin D'Costa (b. 1958) works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Cambridge and at Birmingham under John Hick. His career includes posts at West London Institute, Bristol (Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology), and visiting professorships in Rome.

Gavin Flood (b. 1954) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. After studying at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith, he held posts at Lampeter, Stirling, Oxford, Campion Hall, and Yale-NUS College.

Gaya Charan Tripathi (b. 1939) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ulrich Schneider from around 1963 to 1966 and served as Principal of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha from circa 1977 to 1998.
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indologist who is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student under Claire Maes and as a faculty member at the University of Tübingen.
Geir Heierstad is an Indologist and interdisciplinary scholar who served as Director at Oslo Metropolitan University in 2014 and is attested as faculty at the University of Oslo in 2026.

Gelek is a Tibetologist who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He has also held visiting positions at the University of California and the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche (1939–2017) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Trained at Drepung Monastery and other institutions under masters including Ling and Trijang Rinpoches, he directed Tibet House in New Delhi and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, receiving instruction from traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Toyo Bunko (~1965–1975) and Kokugakuin University (2006).
Gendun Chopel (1903–1951) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung monasteries, learning under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
Gendun Chophel (1903–1951) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso from circa 1928 to 1934 and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.
Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He founded several centres, including Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, where he served as abbot and retreat master from circa 1977 to 1997.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University under multiple teachers, he served as a professor at Otani University, a lecturer at Osaka University, and held visiting professorships at Hamburg and Harvard.
Genro (1717–1789) was a Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and served as first seat (daiza) at Myōshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1934 and later served as a professor there from circa 1962 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned undergraduate and doctoral degrees at Waseda University and held posts at Kokushikan University and Rissho University, where he became professor emeritus.
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Toyo University and became a dharma heir under Sogaku Harada.
Genzao (d. 1993) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian religious studies. After studying at Stockholm, Copenhagen, and Uppsala under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he served as dean at Uppsala (1937–1973) and led the International Association for the History of Religions.

Geoff Childs is a Tibetologist and historian/archaeologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington studying under Tsetan Chonjore, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Australian National University, and joined Washington University in St. Louis in 2002.
